messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: GPU ECC error rate exceeded threshold on host gpu-node-45 (eu-west-1). Recent Xid errors (Xid 31). Automatic soft-drain started. Investigating.

Ana (SRE): I’m seeing elevated retry rates for a couple of Dedicated pools in eu-west. Metrics: memory-corrected-errors spiking, and 3 distinct Xid 31 events in last 30m.

Jordan (Infra): Confirmed. NVML reports repeated Xid 31 + ECC uncorrectable on GPU 0 of host gpu-node-45. Suspect a flaky card that needs replacement. Planning: cordon & drain node -> migrate workloads -> replace card -> run vendor burn-in + validation -> uncordon. Estimated RTO 2-3 hours if replacement is in-region.

Vik (Ops): For Dedicated customers on reserved capacity, we’ll automatically failover to healthy GPUs in the same pool first. If we can't maintain throughput we’ll spill to burst capacity (if available) or trigger cross-region routing per policy. We should be explicit in customer comms about possible degraded throughput for up to ~30 minutes during the final switchover.

Sarah (Customer Success): I need a short customer-facing blurb we can send to affected Dedicated and Private customers. Key asks: what happened, what we did, immediate impact, expected timeline, mitigation steps, and next steps. Avoid deep technical noise but include an optional technical addendum.

Mike (Eng): Draft suggestion — short and skimmable, include escalation path + contact. Also flag Private (VPC/on-prem) differences (we may need customer-side approval/windows).

Ana (SRE): Draft (technical addendum for CS -> append if customer requests it):
```
Root cause: suspect hardware GPU ECC uncorrectable errors (Xid 31) on host gpu-node-45. Action taken: node soft-drained and running on fallback capacity. Next steps: replace physical GPU and run vendor validation, restore node.
Commands used for drain (internal):
redwoodctl node cordon gpu-node-45
redwoodctl workload migrate --node gpu-node-45 --grace-period 120
redwoodctl node replace-hw --node gpu-node-45 --component gpu0
Validation: vendor burn-in + perf sanity tests (2h)
```

Vik (Ops): Customer-facing draft — concise, please edit: 
"Hello — We’re reaching out to let you know we detected a hardware issue affecting GPUs in eu-west-1 that impacted a subset of Dedicated/Private nodes. Our platform automatically routed traffic to healthy capacity; some workloads experienced brief degraded throughput while we migrated tasks. We have scheduled a hardware replacement and verification for the affected host and expect the operation to complete within 2–4 hours. No customer data was exposed or lost. If you operate a Private/on-prem deployment, our team will coordinate a maintenance window with you — estimated 3–4 hours including onsite replacement and validation. We’ll update you when the node is back in service and provide a short incident summary. If you have concerns or critical SLAs impacted, please reply or open a ticket and we’ll prioritize a mitigation plan. — Redwood Inference Ops"

Sarah (Customer Success): Nice — two edits: (1) replace "degraded throughput" with "briefly reduced throughput for some requests" and (2) add an explicit ETA for the customer-facing notification follow-up: "We will send an update within 60 minutes with progress." Also add contact link to support portal.

Ana (SRE): Updated draft with CS edits and a short technical addendum link: 
"Hello — We’re contacting you because one of the GPUs in eu-west-1 showed hardware ECC/Xid errors. Our system automatically moved work to healthy GPUs; as a result, some requests briefly experienced reduced throughput. We have scheduled a hardware replacement and verification for the affected host and expect the operation to complete within 2–4 hours. No customer data was exposed or lost. For Private/on-prem deployments we will coordinate a maintenance window with your team — estimated 3–4 hours for replacement and verification. We will send an update within 60 minutes with progress and a short incident summary once complete. For urgent SLA impacts, please contact our support portal: https://support.redwood.ai — Redwood Inference Ops"

Jordan (Infra): Approved. One note: if replacement parts are not available in region, fallback will be to reallocate from another zone which could extend ETA to 6–8 hours. Add that as a contingency note in the CS ticket but not in the initial customer-facing short message.

Vik (Ops): Also include brief internal runbook steps for CS escalation (so CS knows when to loop in account execs): severity threshold (>=10% request error or customer complaint escalates), contact oncall and infra lead, propose credit/remediation options.

Sarah (Customer Success): Final: I’ll send the concise message now to the affected Dedicated accounts and begin scheduled outreach for Private customers. I’ll attach the technical addendum for customers who want it and include the ETA note for the 60-minute update. Sending at 15:20 UTC. :thumbsup:

Ana (SRE): Post-action checklist for thread record: 1) attach GPU vendor logs + NVML dumps, 2) note replacement part serial, 3) record post-replacement perf benchmarks, 4) update the incident tracker with timeline and lesson.

Mike (Eng): For Private customers who require an on-prem replacement, we will need customer decor approval to open their rack and swap the card. Suggest CS coordinate and copy infra lead to the calendar invite.

Jordan (Infra): I’ll kick off the replacement request to the hardware vendor now and update this thread with ETAs.

oncall-bot: NOTE: node gpu-node-45 has been set to DRAINING by Ana (SRE) at 1718203200. Current migration: 68/68 workloads moved.

Sarah (Customer Success): Thanks team — closing loop on comms. Please post any updates here and I’ll relay to customers.
